peerMapping.justification: The construction is an AI and mega-cap growth sleeve rather than a generic basket. Nasdaq-100 returns are driven mainly by a small group of long-duration platform and semiconductor names, so the sleeve weights NVDA, Microsoft, Alphabet, Apple, Amazon, Meta, Micron, and Tesla according to economic comparability while using the displayed 24-hour perp liquidity stated in USD millions as a constraint. Micron has very deep displayed liquidity at 21.299 USD millions but receives only 0.07 because memory supply is an input-cost channel for the AI-hardware complex, not a full substitute for the whole index. Amazon is highly relevant through cloud and consumer-cycle exposure but is capped at 0.10 because its displayed liquidity is only 1.649 USD millions. The SP500 hedge is a correlated equity-beta substitute: it should offset part of broad index risk, but it will not perfectly protect a pure Nasdaq-100 technology concentration drawdown.

peers.name: NVIDIA
peers.reason: NVIDIA is the clearest common-factor peer: AI accelerator revenue, data-center capital expenditure, and high-beta growth positioning transmit directly into Nasdaq-100 leadership. Its weight is highest despite only 4.508 USD millions of displayed liquidity because comparability is strongest.

peers.name: Microsoft
peers.reason: Microsoft shares the same cloud, enterprise software, and AI-capex monetization channel, and its large capitalization makes it a core long-duration growth exposure inside the Nasdaq-100 rather than an unrelated diversification name.

peers.name: Apple
peers.reason: AAPL is a core Nasdaq-100 mega-cap growth exposure tied to consumer hardware, services margins, buybacks, and the same real-rate valuation channel as the index. It is less purely tied to AI servers than NVDA or MSFT, and displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 2.905 USD millions, supporting a large but not top weight.

peers.name: Alphabet
peers.reason: Alphabet combines digital-advertising cyclicality with cloud and AI infrastructure exposure; with 4.758 USD millions of displayed liquidity it can carry a slightly higher weight than Apple while still explaining the same risk-on growth channel.

peers.name: Amazon
peers.reason: AMZN captures the same cloud and AI infrastructure cycle through AWS plus the US consumer spending channel that matters for Nasdaq-100 earnings breadth. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 1.649 USD millions, thinner than the other mega caps, so the weight is moderated.

peers.name: Meta Platforms
peers.reason: Meta Platforms exposes the block to advertising cyclicality plus AI model and recommendation monetization, which is a common earnings lever for the mega-cap growth factor that dominates Nasdaq-100.

peers.name: Micron Technology
peers.reason: MU adds the AI memory and storage cycle that feeds the same data-center buildout as the Nasdaq-100's semiconductor complex, but with more commodity-like memory pricing beta than the platform mega caps. Displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 21.299 USD millions, the deepest in this peer set, so it receives a liquidity-aware boost above what index size alone would imply.

peers.name: Tesla
peers.reason: Tesla is a high-beta mega-cap growth name in the same risk-on equity channel, and 4.787 USD millions of displayed liquidity is deep relative to other single-name peers.

primary_index_hedge.name: S&P 500
primary_index_hedge.reason: SP500 is the cleanest primary risk hedge for XYZ100 because it shares the same US equity risk-on/risk-off channel, the same dollar and interest-rate discounting channel, and the same broad earnings cycle, while diluting the Nasdaq-100's extra concentration in mega-cap AI and semiconductor names. Its displayed 24-hour perp liquidity is 50.729 USD millions, close to XYZ100 at 52.585 USD millions, so the hedge can be sized with similar depth.

peerMapping.historyMethod: daily-rebalanced peer spot total returns using the fixed Kimi weights; unavailable pre-listing peers are omitted and remaining weights renormalized once at least three peers exist; the browser rebases the basket to the target spot level at the first shared date of each selected chart range

liveSplice.method: current TradeXYZ perp mid divided by that peer's TradeXYZ close on its latest spot date; available Kimi weights renormalized and applied as a one-period return from the published peer spot endpoint; USD cash close is retained for disclosure but never mixed with a differently scaled perp contract

underlierSelection.method: highest summed live contract volume; open interest and contract count break ties

model.name: ATM-straddle-implied lognormal distribution
model.description: Each target uses the nearest paired liquid ATM call and put. Their combined ask implies the expiration distribution shown on the chart.
model.measure: option-implied, not a historical or physical forecast
